response.rationale: R4 best integrates the full temporal and symptomatic profile: intensely pruritic, recurrent 3-day outbreaks, well-defined erythematous papules/plaques, and spontaneous resolution without residual injury, with symmetric anterior thigh distribution and annular/polycyclic morphology with central clearing compatible with urticaria multiforme. R1 captures morphology and purpuric edges but lacks the pruritic, recurrent, self-resolving temporal pattern typical of urticaria; EM would not resolve in 3-day outbreaks without residual injury. R3 is disfavored by normal inflammatory/complement labs and absence of systemic symptoms or residual injury. R2 is a purely descriptive label.

rejected.why: Shares annular/polycyclic morphology and purpuric edges, but misses the intensely pruritic, recurrent 3-day outbreaks and spontaneous resolution without residual injury; EM is less pruritic and typically lasts longer.
Only supports annular morphology; lacks pruritus, recurrence, resolution, purpuric edges, and distribution, making it a non-specific descriptive label.
Purpuric edges and papules/plaques are present, but normal inflammatory/complement labs, absence of systemic symptoms, and spontaneous resolution without residual injury argue against vasculitis.
